name: Curl Up and Die
label: Revelation
lede: Self-described nerds from Las Vegas who played the desert off a generator, got booed for telling moshers not to punch girls, and named a seven-minute song after a Carson Daly lookalike contest.

eras.title: Generators in the desert
eras.text: Las Vegas had almost nowhere for an all-ages metallic hardcore band to play. So Curl Up and Die played frat houses, a BMX crew's place, a racquetball court and the open desert, and learned to run.

years.h: Curl Up and Die form in Las Vegas
years.p: Singer [[Mike Minnick|71288642-a810-4d9c-880f-09aecf594629]], who'd drummed in Vegas grindcore band The Weirding Way, starts Curl Up and Die with guitarist Matt Fuchs and drummer Jesse Fitts. Demo tapes follow in 1998 and 1999.

years.cap: Curl Up and Die · via Discogs
years.h: Curl Up and Die's desert shows, run off a generator
years.p: With no all-ages venue in Las Vegas, Curl Up and Die buy a generator and play the desert. Matt Fuchs remembers running across it with his amp, the police behind him.
years.xp:
The house shows weren't calmer. At a frat party the crowd expected pop-punk. In a West Side mansion they set up in a racquetball court until the homeowner's father came down to confront them.

At one Halloween show the host's father body-slammed Mike Minnick, who was dressed as Tigger at the time.

years.h: The Only Good Bug Is a Dead Bug EP
years.p: Curl Up and Die's first EP, self-released and then picked up by Status Records. The title is a Starship Troopers line; Matt Fuchs later called the record so sloppy, so messy.

eras.title: A geek is a good thing
eras.text: Curl Up and Die were, in their own words, a bunch of weird, nerdy dudes, in a scene that didn't reward it. Revelation signed them anyway, and they went east to Converge's guitarist to make a debut full of sci-fi samples and very long song titles.

years.h: Status Records releases Curl Up and Die's 1998
years.p: Status collects Curl Up and Die's early recordings as 1998.

years.h: Booed in Las Vegas for asking moshers not to punch girls
years.p: Mike Minnick told Vegas crowds it was fine to mosh but not to punch a girl in the face while she watched the show. People booed. Someone once squirted ketchup on the Curl Up and Die van.
years.xp:
Minnick says the Vegas scene splintered along subculture lines and a band of nerds didn't fit any of them.

At a bar-and-arcade venue a security guard maced the band's friends. Matt Fuchs, whose guitar had been damaged, punched the guard. When the police sorted it out, the charges went against the guard.

q: A geek is a good thing.
years.src: Wikipedia · Exclaim! · Revelation Records pressing history
years.p: Curl Up and Die's debut album, recorded at God City Studio with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]. Sixteen tracks, some seconds long, two past seven minutes.
years.xp:
The long ones: You'd Be Cuter if I Shot You in the Face (8:10) and Rich Hall (Runner Up in a Carson Daly Lookalike Contest) (7:05). The lineup: Mike Minnick, Matt Fuchs, Ryan Hartery on bass, Jesse Fitts on drums. Revelation's first press was 311 on grey vinyl and 788 on black.

Minnick told Exclaim! the title is about wanting it easier: wanting to be a robot, with no feelings at all.
play: Rich Hall (Runner Up in a Carson Daly Lookalike Contest)

eras.title: The past isn't through with them
eras.text: Two EPs with a joke split between their titles, a second album the band still calls its favorite era, and then a last show in Anaheim, the room they'd played more than any other outside Vegas.

years.h: We May Be Through with the Past... and But the Past Ain't Through with Us
years.p: Curl Up and Die's two 2003 EPs finish each other's sentence: the first half of the title on Status Records, the second on Revelation.

years.h: The One Above All, the End of All That Is · Revelation
years.p: Curl Up and Die's second and last album, produced by Alex Newport at Hothead Studios with art by Dave Gorum. Matt Fuchs and Mike Minnick call this era their favorite.

years.cap: Curl Up and Die · via Discogs
years.h: Curl Up and Die's last show, at Chain Reaction in Anaheim
years.p: Curl Up and Die end at Chain Reaction, the Anaheim club they'd played more than anywhere but Las Vegas. Mike Minnick moves to Chicago and Jesse Fitts loses interest in metalcore.

eras.title: It always got hung up on a drummer
eras.text: Every reunion attempt stalled on the same problem: who plays drums. When Matt Fuchs's friend from junior high said yes, Curl Up and Die came back to the same Anaheim room where they'd stopped.

years.h: Curl Up and Die miss Revelation's 25th anniversary
years.p: Curl Up and Die were announced for Revelation Records' 25th anniversary shows before logistics were confirmed, and pulled out. Distance, with Mike Minnick in Chicago, sank it.

years.cap: Curl Up and Die · via Discogs
q: I don't play a show just to play a show.
years.h: Curl Up and Die reunite at Chain Reaction, and it sells out
years.p: Fourteen years after their last show in the same Anaheim room, Curl Up and Die return with Keil Corcoran on drums, with Taken, Seizures and Regional Justice Center. The show sells out.
years.xp:
Mike Minnick expected little and got what he called something far beyond anything he'd anticipated. They played their longest set ever, from every era. Matt Fuchs's eyes were burning afterward, possibly from the rose water someone was spritzing.

The band's rule for the new lineup: members had to be friends first. Fuchs had known Corcoran since junior high.

years.h: Curl Up and Die's Vegas homecoming at the Bunkhouse Saloon
years.p: Curl Up and Die play Las Vegas again, at the Bunkhouse Saloon. They joked about doing it in the desert instead, like the old days.

years.h: Writing new Curl Up and Die songs in Joshua Tree
years.p: The band plans writing sessions at a remote house in Joshua Tree. Matt Fuchs says the new songs run from thrash to industrial; Mike Minnick calls them Curl Up and Die, just years later.
